post.description:
Accepts a certificate enrollment request and begins processing it.

Allowed private key types:
- RSA (OID: 1.2.840.113549.1.1.1), key length equal to 2048 bits,
- EC (elliptic curve-based keys, OID: 1.2.840.10045.2.1), NIST P-256 curve (secp256r1)

EC keys are recommended.

Allowed signature algorithms:
- RSA PKCS#1 v1.5,
- RSA PSS,
- ECDSA (signature format compliant with RFC 3279)

Allowed hash functions used for CSR signature:
- SHA1,
- SHA256,
- SHA384,
- SHA512

> More information:
> - [Submitting certificate enrollment](https://github.com/CIRFMF/ksef-docs/blob/main/certyfikaty-KSeF.md#4-wys%C5%82anie-wniosku-certyfikacyjnego)

post.summary: Grant permissions to natural persons to work in KSeF
post.description:
The method allows granting permissions to work in KSeF to the person specified in the request  
in the current context.
            
The request specifies the permissions to be granted from the set:  
- **InvoiceWrite** – invoice issuing,  
- **InvoiceRead** – invoice viewing,  
- **CredentialsManage** – permission management,  
- **CredentialsRead** – permission viewing,  
- **Introspection** – session history viewing and UPO generation,  
- **SubunitManage** – subordinate unit management,  
- **EnforcementOperations** – performing enforcement operations.
            
The method allows selecting any combination of the above permissions.  
The **EnforcementOperations** permission can be granted only when  
the context subject has the role **EnforcementAuthority** (enforcement authority)  
or **CourtBailiff** (court bailiff).

> More information:
> - [Granting permissions](https://github.com/CIRFMF/ksef-docs/blob/main/uprawnienia.md#nadawanie-uprawnie%C5%84-osobom-fizycznym-do-pracy-w-ksef)

**Required permissions**: `CredentialsManage`.

post.description:
The method allows granting administrator permissions to the entity or natural person indicated in the request in the context of:  
- the indicated NIP of the subordinate entity – only if the entity of the current login context has the role of superior entity:
  - **LocalGovernmentUnit** 
  - **VatGroupUnit**  
- the indicated or created internal identifier  
            
Along with creating the administrator of the subordinate unit, an internal identifier is created consisting of the NIP number of the login context entity and 5 digits uniquely identifying the internal unit.
The last digit must be a correct check digit, which is calculated according to the algorithm below.

The algorithm uses alternating weights (1×, 3×, 1×, 3×, ...), sums the results and returns the remainder from division by 10.

Example:
- Input: "6824515772-1234" (without check digit)
- Position 0 (1st digit): 6 × 1 = 6
- Position 1 (2nd digit): 8 × 3 = 24
- Position 2 (3rd digit): 2 × 1 = 2
- Position 3 (4th digit): 4 × 3 = 12
- Position 4 (5th digit): 5 × 1 = 5
- Position 5 (6th digit): 1 × 3 = 3
- Position 6 (7th digit): 5 × 1 = 5
- Position 7 (8th digit): 7 × 3 = 21
- Position 8 (9th digit): 7 × 1 = 7
- Position 9 (10th digit): 2 × 3 = 6
- Position 10 (11th digit): 1 × 1 = 1
- Position 11 (12th digit): 2 × 3 = 6
- Position 12 (13th digit): 3 × 1 = 3
- Position 13 (14th digit): 4 × 3 = 12
- Sum: 6 + 24 + 2 + 12 + 5 + 3 + 5 + 21 + 7 + 6 + 1 + 6 + 3 + 12 = 113
- Check digit (15th digit): 113 % 10 = 3

The request also provides the name of this unit.  
            
Subordinate unit administrator permissions include:  
- **CredentialsManage** – permission management  
            
The method automatically grants the above permission without the need to specify it in the request.
            
> More information:
> - [Granting permissions](https://github.com/CIRFMF/ksef-docs/blob/main/uprawnienia.md#nadanie-uprawnie%C5%84-administratora-podmiotu-podrz%C4%99dnego)

**Required permissions**: `SubunitManage`.

post.description:
The method allows granting administrator permissions to the entity or natural person indicated in the request in a composite context consisting of the NIP identifier of the current context entity and the EU VAT number of the EU entity indicated in the request.  
Along with creating the EU entity administrator, a composite context is created consisting of the NIP number of the login context entity and the indicated EU VAT identification number of the EU entity.  
The request also provides the name and address of the EU entity.  
            
The only way to identify the authorized party is the qualified certificate fingerprint:  
- electronic signature certificate for natural persons  
- electronic seal certificate for entities  
            
EU entity administrator permissions include:  
- **VatEuManage** – permission management within the EU entity  
- **InvoiceWrite** – issuing invoices  
- **InvoiceRead** – viewing invoices  
- **Introspection** – viewing session history  
            
The method automatically grants all the above permissions without the need to specify them in the request.
            
> More information:
> - [Granting permissions](https://github.com/CIRFMF/ksef-docs/blob/main/uprawnienia.md#nadanie-uprawnie%C5%84-administratora-podmiotu-unijnego)

Method allows reading own permissions of authenticated API client in the current login context.  

 The following permissions are returned in the response:  
 - granted directly in the current context  
 - granted by parent entity  
 - granted indirectly, if the login context entity is an intermediary or target entity in the permission  
 - granted to entity for invoice handling by another entity, if the authenticated entity has ownership permissions in the current context  

 Permissions returned by the operation include:  
 - **CredentialsManage** – permission management  
 - **CredentialsRead** – permission viewing  
 - **InvoiceWrite** – invoice issuance  
 - **InvoiceRead** – invoice viewing  
 - **Introspection** – session history viewing  
 - **SubunitManage** – subordinate entity management  
 - **EnforcementOperations** – enforcement operations execution

 The list of retrieved permissions can be of two types:  
 - List of all permissions valid in the current login context (used when an administrator wants to review permissions of all users in the current context)  
 - List of all permissions granted in the current context by the authenticated API client (used when an administrator wants to review the list of permissions they have granted in the current context)  

 For the first list (valid permissions), the response includes:  
 - persons and entities that can work in the current context excluding persons authorized indirectly  
 - persons authorized indirectly by the entity of the current context  

 For the second list (granted permissions), the response includes:  
 - permissions granted directly for work in the current context or in subordinate unit contexts  
 - permissions granted indirectly for handling clients of the current context entity

 - **CredentialsManage** – permission management  
 - **CredentialsRead** – permission viewing  
 - **InvoiceWrite** – invoice issuing  
 - **InvoiceRead** – invoice viewing

 - **SubunitManage** – subordinate entity management  
 - **EnforcementOperations** – enforcement operations

 - **authorIdentifier** – identifier of the person who granted the permission  
 - **authorizedIdentifier** – identifier of the authorized person or entity  
 - **targetIdentifier** – identifier of the target entity for indirectly granted permissions  
 - **permissionTypes** – list of permission types to search for  
 - **permissionState** – permission status

tags.name: Certificates
tags.description:
KSeF certificate is a digital identity credential for an entity, issued by the KSeF system upon request from an authenticated entity. 
This certificate can be used for:

- authentication in the KSeF system,
- performing operations in offline mode, including issuing invoices directly in the user's application.

**Note**: Applying for a KSeF certificate is only possible after authentication using a signature (XAdES). Authentication using a KSeF system token does not allow submitting an application.

tags.name: Test data
tags.description:
API for creating and managing test data such as entities, natural persons and permissions. Possible entities to create are: enforcement authority, VAT group and local government units. For natural persons, you can specify whether the person is a bailiff. The functionality of granting and receiving permissions aims to replicate the operation of the ZAW-FA form in the test environment.

More information:
- [Test scenarios](https://github.com/CIRFMF/ksef-docs/blob/main/dane-testowe-scenariusze.md)

tags.name: KSeF Tokens
tags.description:
KSeF Token is a unique, generated authentication identifier that — on par with [qualified electronic signature](https://github.com/CIRFMF/ksef-docs/blob/main/uwierzytelnianie.md#21-uwierzytelnianie-kwalifikowanym-podpisem-elektronicznym) — enables [authentication](https://github.com/CIRFMF/ksef-docs/blob/main/uwierzytelnianie.md#22-uwierzytelnianie-tokenem-ksef) to the KSeF API. KSeF Token is issued with an immutable set of permissions defined upon its creation; any modification of these permissions requires generating a new token. > **Warning!**
> KSeF Token serves as a **confidential authentication secret** — it should be stored exclusively in a trusted and secure repository. More information: - [KSeF Token](https://github.com/CIRFMF/ksef-docs/blob/main/tokeny-ksef.md)

tags.name: Getting access
tags.description:
Authentication in the KSeF API 2.0 system is a mandatory step that must be performed before accessing protected system resources. This process is based on **obtaining an access token** (```accessToken```) in ```JWT``` format, which is then used to authorize API operations.

> More information:
> - [Authentication](https://github.com/CIRFMF/ksef-docs/blob/main/uwierzytelnianie.md)
